image-splitter.formula:
tile_w = floor(width / cols),  tile_h = floor(height / rows)
last column width  = width − tile_w × (cols − 1)
last row height     = height − tile_h × (rows − 1)
tiles = rows × cols

keyFacts: The image is sliced into an exact rows × columns grid — up to 10 × 10 = 100 tiles.

Each tile is named by its grid position, like photo-r2c3.png.

image-splitter.workedExample:
A 1200 × 800 px photo split into 3 columns × 2 rows:
tile_w = floor(1200 / 3) = 400 px
tile_h = floor(800 / 2) = 400 px
tiles = 3 × 2 = 6, each exactly 400 × 400 px
A 1000 × 800 px photo into 3 columns: tile_w = floor(1000 / 3) = 333 px, and the last column gets 1000 − 333 × 2 = 334 px — no pixel lost.
